arguments.key_range: A +0x8 = range start, A +0x10 = range end; the key slice is start..end-8 (an 8-byte trailer is stripped, as in the #1985 entry check)
arguments.register: rdi = host; rsi = key-range argument A; rdx, rcx, r8, r9 = further caller arguments (spilled to stack slots)
arguments.stack_args: 0x10, 0x18 (output pointer for the max-update), 0x20 (output pointer for the probe-miss sentinel), 0x28 (thunk options argument), 0x30 (low byte forwarded to the thunk), 0x38, 0x40, 0x48 (low byte forwarded to the driver)

census.note: every direct call site was confirmed as a real call instruction in objdump output, not only as a byte-pattern match

component: probe-gated lookup (node #94 0x516ca20) with its member resolution, probe filter and driver call

driver_0x516c7e0.consumer_link: the driver itself calls the 0x516b130 Seek implementation (call at 0x516c95f) plus iterator virtuals; its own full semantics are a separate item (the Seek is the suggested next phased item) and are NOT claimed here beyond the call-site contract
driver_0x516c7e0.dispatch_note: the driver compares a +0x98 field against the GOT slot 0x57783c0 value 0x5164750 (RELATIVE addend, pinned); the compared function itself is not decoded here
driver_0x516c7e0.outputs: after the call, -0x82 is the function's return value and -0x81 gates the status-6 install; a nonzero -0x82 skips the install and goes to the epilogue
driver_0x516c7e0.register_args: rdi = host; rsi = key-range argument A; rdx = *stack-arg-0x18 object; rcx = low byte of stack arg 0x48; r8 = stack arg 0x38; r9 = stack arg 0x40

epilogue.order: perf +0x120 counter (gated as above); return value = the -0x82 byte; when the member is non-null its +0x8 virtual is called (release); when the timer start is nonzero the timer destructor runs; stack check, then return
epilogue.return_value: the -0x82 byte: 0 on the early-gate and probe-miss paths, the driver's out flag on the driver path

gate.closed_behavior: when host +0xc18 is null the function returns 0 immediately: no perf prologue, no member resolution, no probe, no driver call, no member release

member_resolution.max_update: the transform result is compared against *output (stack arg 0x18): when *output >= result nothing is updated; otherwise *output = result and, when the r8 string argument is non-null, the string is replaced wholesale with the looked-up pair
member_resolution.null_member: a null member skips the whole key-handling block and rejoins at the probe setup with the original range
member_resolution.pair_lookup: index = (member +0x90 pointer - member +0x68 table +0x18 array) / 8; pair = 16-byte entry at table +0x30 + index * 16; the string replace is std::string::replace(0, old size, pair pointer, pair length)
member_resolution.thunk: 0x516aa20 (built in #2003): returns null when the options argument +0x35 is nonzero or host +0xa60 is nonzero; otherwise tail-jumps to the #2003 sharded access 0x516a390 with (host, options, (word at (A +0x10 pointer) - 8) >> 8, low byte of stack arg 0x30)
member_resolution.transform: 0x51922d0 (member, key slice) — see transform record below

miss_path.sentinel: the stack-arg-0x20 output pointee is written -1 (all bits set)
miss_path.status_gate: the -0x81 byte (on this path still the r9-object-first-byte == 6 flag from probe setup) selects the status install; when it is 0 the function goes straight to the epilogue
miss_path.status_install: when -0x81 is set, the move helper 0x5164ce0 moves the record {header bytes 06 00 00 00 00 00, null pointer} into the r9 object, unless the r9 object's first byte is already 2, in which case the install is skipped; the caller's post-move delete[] of the temporary pointer is dead on this path because the move zeroes the temporary pointer (see move_helper)

move_helper_0x5164ce0.behavior: copies 6 header bytes and the pointer from source to destination, zeroes the source header and pointer one field at a time, and frees the destination's previous pointer with operator delete[] when it is non-null; a source equal to the destination returns immediately

perf_counters.counter_block: TLS-0x350; the timer record's counter field points at block + 0x118
perf_counters.gate: each counter increment is gated on the TLS perf byte being above 1 (after the perf_level slot check and getter call)
perf_counters.plus_0x200: incremented on the driver-call entry that follows a probe hit (the 0x516cea8 entry); the probe-skip and virtual-false driver entries bypass it

probe.direct_variant: the range start and the probe length are hashed directly, with no virtual calls
probe.hash: 0x5422e70 (pointer, length, seed 0xbc9f1d34) — internals not claimed here; the same helper and seed as the #1994 probe
probe.loop: base = (table count * hash32) >> 32; words = table +0x8; round k tests words[base XOR k] against the two-bit mask (bits (hash product & 63) and ((hash product >> 6) & 63)) of the 64-bit product hash32 * 0x9e3779b97f4a7c13, rotated right 12 after each passing round; round 0 is always tested even when the rounds field (table +0x4) is 0; a failing round is a miss, an exhausted loop is a hit exactly when the last word holds both mask bits
probe.miss: the probe-miss path runs (see miss_path); the driver is NOT called
probe.mode_flag: host +0x30 byte: nonzero selects the direct-hash variant, zero selects the virtual variant
probe.slice: probe slice = {range start, (range end - range start - 8) - (host +0x10 object) +0x28} — the same target_len - 8 - holder +0x28 form as the #1994 seek gate
probe.table_field: host +0xc60; a null table skips the probe and goes straight to the driver call
probe.virtual_variant: the host +0xc58 object +0xa0 virtual is called with the probe slice; false skips the probe and goes to the driver; true calls the +0x98 virtual, whose (pointer, length) result is hashed

timer.destructor: 0x5165320 (91 bytes, FDE 0xf7cd98) — called in the epilogue exactly when the start value is nonzero, as read in #1994 (it adds the elapsed time to the +0x138 counter); its internals are not re-decoded here
timer.install: only when the TLS byte at fs:0-0x10a8 is above 2: the object comes from 0x5242050 and the start value from its +0xa0 virtual; the counter block (TLS-0x350 + 0x118) is set on both paths
timer.perf_prologue: 0x52cd6e0 is called unconditionally after the host +0xc18 gate; when the perf_level slot 0x5777ef8 (GLOB_DAT) is nonzero the TLS getter 0x56606a0 is called first
timer.record: stack record at -0x60: flag byte (TLS perf byte > 2, via seta), object at +8, start value at +16, counter block at +24, zero at +32

transform_0x51922d0.comparator: the member +0x40 object dispatches: its +0xd0 virtual is compared against the GOT slot 0x5777bf8 value 0x4fa7de0 (RELATIVE addend, pinned); equal takes the +0x10 virtual on the +0x20 subobject with (pair, slice), unequal takes the +0xd0 virtual with (object, pair, 1, slice, 1); a comparator result above 0 returns 0, otherwise the function returns the qword at *member +0x90
transform_0x51922d0.steps: calls 0x51910a0 first (effect unresolved, see unknowns); when the member vtable +0x10 slot differs from 0x518e2c0 that virtual is called with (member, slice) and a false result returns 0, a true result falls into the table walk; when the slot equals 0x518e2c0 the walk runs directly
transform_0x51922d0.walk: table = member +0x68; null table returns 0; table +0x8 equal to the member +0x88 pointer returns 0 (empty); entry = table +0x18 + (index object +0x28) * 8; member +0x90 equal to that entry returns 0 (end sentinel)

unknowns: the host object's identity and the meaning of its +0xc18, +0xc60, +0xc58, +0x30 and +0x10 fields beyond their observed roles
the effect of the transform's first call 0x51910a0
the exact meaning of the (pointer, length) pair the transform's comparator receives and of the member +0x40 object
the enum meaning of the r9 object's first byte (6 selects the miss-path install, 2 skips it) and of the installed record's 6-byte header beyond its literal bytes
the driver's own semantics beyond its call-site contract and its Seek call; the 0x516b130 Seek implementation itself is the suggested next item
the hash helper 0x5422e70 internals (verbatim excerpt included; only its call signature and seed are claimed)
